sections.content:
590,650 people

were counted on the census as "other administrative occupations" in England and Wales in March 2021.

This makes this type of work the fourth most common occupation reported on the census.

People who do this type of work may are responsible for recording, filing and sharing information for a business, organisation or individual not elsewhere classified.

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "other administrative occupations" there were more women than men (81.5% compared with 18.5%).

This means "other administrative occupations" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "administrative occupations".

Men made up 18.5% and women made up 81.5% of "other administrative occupations"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "other administrative occupations" included:

  • care escorts
  • houseparents and residential wardens
  • office managers

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "other administrative occupations" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 50 to 54 years. Of the whole working population 11.7% were aged 50 to 54 years. For people working as "other administrative occupations", 11.9% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "other administrative occupations" was 16 to 19 years.

Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "other administrative occupations" included:

  • metal working machine operatives
  • metal working production and maintenance fitters
  • welding trades

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

We can look at who worked as "other administrative occupations" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged under 30 years old, we see there is a higher proportion of men with this occupation than women.

The percentage of men and women who are "other administrative occupations" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "other administrative occupations", 11.7% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (54.9% compared with 45.1%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (94%) than self-employed (6%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
